feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the experience is coherent, relevant, and supported by concrete platform, scale, and leadership details. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary establish a focused niche in digital platforms, governance, communications systems, and AI-enabled experiences.  
- Strong credibility: long progression at NACo shows advancement, leadership growth, and ownership of substantial initiatives like a 10,000+ page migration and analytics modernization.  
- Good technical breadth: combines strategy, editorial operations, CMS/platform delivery, analytics, and multimedia in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results would strengthen them (e.g., engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption rates, cost savings, search performance).  
- Reduce duplication: “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” “Core Competencies,” and “Recent Projects” overlap; consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; use either “organization-wide”/“organisation-wide” consistently; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma. No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstraction: replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a scale cue from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Prioritize the most relevant leadership areas: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search; multimedia can be shortened or moved later.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, digital governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Built and scaled enterprise platforms and editorial systems supporting complex, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, expanded analytics infrastructure, and AI-enabled search and discovery experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search and discovery.”
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered in skills and experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinctive and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording for cleaner scanability.
- Replace “communications operations” with “communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and performance infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, prioritize the most current differentiators first: AI-enabled search, enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, and governance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already repeated in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills’ “Public-sector and advocacy messaging”; use one phrasing consistently.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently reads like a second summary of the NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes, formats, or scope will make the footer feel additive rather than repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Increase specificity where possible: name the audience, scale, platform, or deliverable type (for example, “Drupal 10 microsite,” “conference installation,” “legislative search”).
- Use stronger action/result framing: “Launched,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Produced,” and end with the value delivered.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent NACo experience bullets; consider reframing them as “Selected projects” with unique implementation details not already covered.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; keep it, as it adds range beyond the core experience section.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Make it sharper by framing this as post-staff strategic/technical consulting with clearer scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with the consulting angle and client scope: “Advise the National Association of Counties on digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for enterprise web and campaign initiatives.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused lines; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel operations.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, publishers supported, traffic/users affected, toolkit downloads, search improvement metrics, or workflow time saved.
- Tighten technical phrasing: replace “Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting” with “Built and optimized Drupal campaign experiences, front-end components, and CMS solutions for public-facing properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording repeats website governance, analytics, and communications operations already covered in the 2022–2024 director role.
- Microsites and AI search also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you add distinct results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and audience growth.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing, especially for email/social/video/governance: growth %, production volume, cost savings, faster publishing, improved reporting adoption, reduced vendor reliance.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels...” with specifics on scale, performance, or strategic change rather than generic oversight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, analytics and studio buildout.
- Video expansion also appears elsewhere; here, emphasize building the in-house studio and organizational capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as support than impact. Tighten it to emphasize what changed under your leadership at this level: channel ownership, recurring products, and workflow improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video point: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” are vague and low-impact; use direct action verbs.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the Director of Digital Media role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership capabilities not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “publishing strategy,” which better matches the CV’s governance/systems emphasis.
- If space allows, align one phrase to measurable scope from recent roles, e.g., “Enterprise web and content leadership for 10,000+ page, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially duplicate Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced throughout NACo experience; keep only if you remove a more repetitive line.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long list to a sharper, impact-oriented grouping: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they are less evidenced in recent experience than Drupal, CMS modernization, and AI search.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, use “Front-end web implementation” instead of listing all languages, since the detailed stack already appears later.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats language from Core Competencies and Recent Projects.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity” then “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Possible rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory there.
- “Performance analysis” may overlap with broader digital strategy unless tied clearly to analytics/optimization.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it sharper, more senior, and tied to the most recent/highest-impact multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution**
- If space allows, add one impact cue rather than only tools: **Built and operated an in-house broadcast studio supporting advocacy programming and event production**
- Keep terms outcome-oriented; “video production and editing” is broad, while “broadcast-quality video production” better matches the Director-level experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This repeats **“Multimedia production and livestream operations”** in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; combine to avoid listing the same capability twice.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add context on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming for precision: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- If you want more impact, replace the plain list with: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed list in one place only.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so avoid repeating that phrase here unless tied to a measurable result.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not a repeat of broader skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize hands-on execution tools rather than basic languages alone.
- Suggested rewrite: **Front-End & Technical Implementation:** JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/specialization: add qualifiers like “custom front-end enhancements,” “serverless scripting,” or “deployment automation.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for cleaner, more senior phrasing unless ATS targeting requires them.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless this section is explicitly for development tooling.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more senior by separating automation tools from collaboration/project platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance to your recent work: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**  
- Move lower-value/older/general tools to the end or remove if space is tight: **Trello • Basecamp**
- If you want more impact, add a short qualifier instead of only listing tools, e.g. **Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier (workflow automation); Jira, Asana (project operations); Slack, Teams (cross-team coordination)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating those exact phrases elsewhere.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if they support a broader workflow/collaboration framing.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/ownership already shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations and member engagement without repeating newsletter details from work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something broader and cleaner, e.g. **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**.
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level of use: **Higher Logic (primary email/member comms platform) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (CRM/email journeys) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**.
- Keep platform names concise; consider shortening **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys** to **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights (Journeys)** for readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like newsletter audience size here; those are already covered in recent NACo experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for the target profile, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo Director role. Tighten it and emphasize methods or outcomes not already stated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Replace with a tighter list: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing**
- Drop **Dashboarding** unless you make it more specific, since Looker Studio and Power BI already imply it; use **KPI reporting** or **performance measurement** if you want a capability label.
- If space allows, add one qualifier for impact: **enterprise analytics reporting** or **behavior analysis**, to better connect tools to senior-level use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills [3]**; consider removing one version or making this section tools-only and the Topline entry capability-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and scope if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size/timing of website refresh, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, email volume, or production cadence.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, split into 2 bullets for readability: one on team/workflow + website refresh, one on content production + informal supervision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching or piloting the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations language; keep this version lighter and more execution-oriented.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim generic support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production, while supporting digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders, or types of projects supported.
- Remove vague phrasing like “contributed to” and “materials”; use stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on research/innovation support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, not broader capabilities already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Tighten to software/platforms and remove workflow-style phrases:  
  **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
- If you want to retain production depth, rename the category to:  
  **Creative Tools & Production Platforms**
- Add only specific platforms not mentioned elsewhere, if accurate, e.g. streaming software or audio tools:  
  **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • OBS/StreamYard/Restream**
